subject: Private fleet weekend patch: handoff notes + emergency evacuation routing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>, ops@acmehealth.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private fleet weekend patch: handoff notes + emergency evacuation routing

Hi Samira / Acme ops team —

As discussed in the runbook review, were planning a low-risk rolling patch of your private fleet this coming weekend (Sat 2025-05-10). This thread is the canonical handoff / emergency routing doc for the window. Key details below so we have a single source of truth.

Planned window
- Start: Sat 2025-05-10 01:00 UTC (Friday 18:00 PT)
- End: Sat 2025-05-10 07:00 UTC (Fri 00:00 PT)
- Target impact: per-node restart for micropatch, ~3–6 minute drain per host; staggered across availability racks.

Version pinning
- Current pinned version: private-2025.04.2
- Patch target: private-2025.04.3 (minor runtime and security fixes)
- We will only unpin if the canary passes health checks for 30 minutes. Pinset will be recorded in SUP-4231.

Rollback / emergency evacuation summary
- If any canary node fails >3 health checks OR KV latency >150ms for 2 consecutive checks, trigger immediate evacuation: follow the Evac Flow (attached evac_flow.png).
- Rollback steps (high level): 1) drain new pods, 2) redeploy pinned image private-2025.04.2 to affected nodes, 3) warm cold caches, 4) validate telemetry. Full step-by-step in Drive link.

Network notes (important)
- We will open ephemeral egress to our control plane for drain signaling (TCP 443 to 52.9.10.12/32).
- Please allow port 9411 (zipkin) for 30m during the canary window so tracing correlates in case of failures.

On-call and owners
- Release lead (Redwood): Marissa Cole (me)
- Network / canary: Jonas Weber
- KMS / secrets: Naomi Feldman
- Emergency rollback owner: Karthik Iyer

Requested actions for Acme:
1) Confirm ops@acmehealth can accept ephemeral egress to 52.9.10.12/32 during the window.
2) Confirm a named point-of-contact (same account) for the Saturday handoff.

Attachments: patch_manifest.yaml (list of images + hashes), evac_flow.png (evacuation flow diagram).

If I dont hear concerns by EOD PT tomorrow I will schedule the handoff meeting and mark SUP-4231 green.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>

Cc: ops@acmehealth.com, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet weekend patch: handoff notes + emergency evacuation routing

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Can we compress the blackout to start at 02:00 UTC instead of 01:00? IT night-shift prefers the later start. That would shrink the planned window by an hour.
- Our security team flagged the open egress IP 52.9.10.12/32; they prefer we put both sides behind a short-lived TLS mTLS cert instead of opening to a public IP. Is that feasible for the control-plane handshake during the drain?

If both answers are yes were comfortable proceeding. I can nominate Daniel (devops-lead@acmehealth.com) as the on-site contact for Saturday.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Ops, AcmeHealth
samira.khan@acmehealth.com

On Mon, May 5, 2025 at 11:03 AM Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
> - Can we compress the blackout to start at 02:00 UTC instead of 01:00?
> - Our security team flagged the open egress IP 52.9.10.12/32; they prefer we put both sides behind a short-lived TLS mTLS cert instead of opening to a public IP.

Samira — both items workable with small caveats. Technical notes for the network team: 
- We can shift to a 02:00 UTC start with the caveat that canary job execution moves later and reduces warm time to 20m instead of 30m. We should still require the 30m metric window for full rollout; recommendation: keep canary at 02:00–02:30, hold 30m, then continue.
- mTLS: Redwood supports ephemeral cert exchange via our control-plane handshake. Well provide a cert bundle a few hours before the window; Acme needs to allow egress to the cert distribution endpoint (https://certs.redwood.com/ephemeral).

Also adding one further request: during the canary, please allow a temporary ACL change to permit internal-only port 9411 from the canary hosts so Zipkin traces can link. Ive attached network-change-template.patch you can use for your firewall team.

If thats all good Ill update SUP-4231 with the shifted timeline.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Systems Engineer, Releases
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet weekend patch: handoff notes + emergency evacuation routing

Folks — quick KMS/secrets note before we finalize: 

- Acmes team scheduled a KMS rotation on 2025-05-09 (our side was not in the loop). If their rotation goes through, anything relying on cached secrets may fail reads for ~5–8 minutes during rewrap. That overlaps with the patch window even if we shift to 02:00 UTC.

Proposed mitigations:
1) If Acme can postpone the KMS rotation by 48 hours, keep the patch this weekend as scheduled.
2) If not, move the patch to the following weekend and well re-run the canary with KMS rewrap test vectors.

Rollback detail suggestion (full step list for SUP-4231):
- Step 0: Stop new canaries from starting (global flag).
- Step 1: Drain traffic off affected nodes.
- Step 2: Redeploy pinned image private-2025.04.2.
- Step 3: Re-seed caches via staged warmup endpoints (warm-1, warm-2).
- Step 4: Validate trace and metric baselines for 10 minutes.
- Step 5: Full re-open if baselines OK.

Im willing to own the KMS checklist if Acme agrees to either postpone the KMS rotation or give us a tight rotation schedule + test keys.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Security & Secrets Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Thanks everyone — good callouts. Final decisions and owners below after syncing with Acme ops this morning (Samira confirmed):

- Window adjusted: start 2025-05-10 02:00 UTC, canary 02:00–02:30, hold 30m, then staged rollout.
- Acme will postpone KMS rotation to 2025-05-12. Naomi will drive the KMS checklist and be available during the hold window.
- Acme to accept ephemeral mTLS cert distribution; Acme ops will confirm egress to https://certs.redwood.com/ephemeral by Friday 17:00 PT.
- Jonas to push network-change-template.patch to Acme firewall team and confirm ACL change for port 9411 pre-window.
- Karthik is the emergency rollback owner and will be on-call for the whole window.

Handoff call scheduled: Fri 2025-05-09 16:00 PT (calendar invite sent) — please join if you own an item above. SUP-4231 updated with the final timeline and the numbered rollback steps Naomi proposed.

If anything changes from Acmes side I will update the runbook link and flag here. Otherwise were good to go.

—
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
